proof_scope: The true sparse-adjoint increment splits as a direct activation sample and a signed sample of the next actual capped Picard increment on the same preimage.

In the staggered depth-zero seed, nonzero bulk direct activation difference at a supported site requires the two adjacent jumps to have total magnitude at least A-M. At deeper fixed repair depth, only the explicit three-height lag set or the true positive cumulative drift above s can support the bulk direct term. The marked direct term is subcritical.

The clipped activation has strictly smaller secant bound q_d on jumps of magnitude at least d for every fixed 0<d<M. Its exact counting energy loss controls the normalized squared mass of those actual jumps and the activation mean square. A corresponding true fixed-point comparison bounds the three-height lag set.

At a critical cap height with the inherited sparse adjoint and actual critical cap rate, a nonzero scaled masked increment forces a critical adjacent two-step loss. Subcritical scaled squared tails at each fixed positive jump size suffice to suppress that increment. A fixed gap from a separately controlled critical endpoint to the actual limit forces such a loss within a fixed successor window.

The unrestricted sparse support and norm implication is false even for the true signed kernel. The generic mean-zero witness imposes no physical activation, repair slopes or actual trajectory and is no counterexample to the target.
